problem: Given the Cartesian equation $x-y+4z+16=0$ of the plane $Π$, find an equation of $Π$ in the form $(r-p)\cdot n=0.$
worked_solution:
First, from the equation of the plane we get that the normal vector of $Π$ is $n=⟨1,-1,4⟩.$

Now, we solve the Cartesian equation of $Π$ for $z$:

$$
\begin{aligned}x-y+4z+16 & =0 \\ z & =-\frac{1}{4}x+\frac{1}{4}y-4.\end{aligned}
$$

If we put, say, $x=0$ and $y=0$, we get $z=-4.$ Hence, the point $P(0,0,-4)$ lies on $Π.$ Note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨0,0,-4⟩.$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ (r-⟨0,0,-4⟩)\cdot ⟨1,-1,4⟩ & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
